title: Tire Check & Seasonal Swap
subtitle: Tires are your only contact with the road — we'll inspect, set pressure, rotate or swap seasons, and know when a shop is smarter.
tone: Coach Mode: calm safety mentor. Celebrate owners who check pressure monthly. Never shame bald tires — escalate clearly. Prefer visuals for tread depth and seasonal swap.
prerequisites: For rotation/swap: jack, stands, torque wrench, and matching lug pattern
tools_checklist: Optional: valve core tool, TPMS relearn tool
parts_checklist: Optional: new TPMS sensors when replacing tires

adaptive_rules.coach_note: Rotate about every 5,000–8,000 miles (often with oil service) unless your manual says otherwise.
If you see regular snow/ice, winter tires (or a dedicated winter set) beat all-seasons once temps stay near freezing.
EVs and many hybrids are heavier — watch inner shoulder wear and keep pressures exact. Use load-rated / OEM-size tires.
Trucks/SUVs that tow or run dirt roads chew edges and rears differently — inspect all four, not just the fronts.
Staggered fitments (different front/rear sizes) often can't cross-rotate. A tire shop prevents wrong-position mounts.
Tread at wear bars, cords showing, sidewall bulge, or a puncture in the sidewall = do not drive far — replace / tow.

steps.title: Tire check — quick win for safety
steps.description: We'll do pressure, tread, and a visual for damage. If you're swapping seasons or rotating, I'll branch you to the right path. You're building a great ownership habit.
steps.safety_warning: A bulge, cut to cord, or rapid hiss means park safe and call for help — don't highway-drive on it.

action_buttons.label: I have a flat / puncture
action_buttons.payload: I have a flat or puncture. Help me decide plug, spare, or tow for my vehicle.

steps.title: Set cold pressure from the placard
steps.description: Use the door-jamb PSI — not the max molded on the sidewall. Check when tires are cold. Adjust all four (and spare if you have one). TPMS light may need a short drive to clear.
steps.safety_warning: Don't 'eyeball' pressure. Underinflation overheats tires; overinflation reduces grip and wears the center.

action_buttons.label: Can't find placard
action_buttons.payload: Help me find the correct cold tire pressure for my year/make/model.

action_buttons.label: TPMS light stays on
action_buttons.payload: TPMS light is on after setting pressures. What should I check next?

variants.description: EV tip: heavy curb weight + wrong PSI shows up as range loss and inner wear. Stick to the placard, including front/rear differences.

steps.title: Tread depth & damage scan
steps.description: Measure the shallowest groove. At wear bars (about 2/32"), plan replacement. Also scan sidewalls for cracks, nails, and bubbles. Note uneven patterns for alignment.
steps.safety_warning: Exposed cord, sidewall bubble, or tread separation — do not drive. Replace or tow.

steps.title: What is the wear telling us?
steps.description: Even wear = good. Both edges low often means underinflation. Center worn = overinflation. One edge / cupping = alignment or suspension. Fix the cause or new tires won't last.

action_buttons.label: Uneven — talk alignment
action_buttons.payload: My tire wear is uneven. Help me decide pressure vs alignment vs rotation next.

steps.title: Rotate, seasonal swap, or shop mount?
steps.description: Pressure + inspect is pure DIY. Rotation or seasonal wheel swaps are DIY if you have stands and a torque wrench. Mounting new tires on rims belongs in a shop with a balancer.
steps.safety_warning: Wrong torque or mismatched sizes front/rear can destabilize the car. When unsure, pay for a mount/balance.

variants.description: Staggered or run-flat setups: confirm rotation pattern (sometimes none). A tire shop avoids putting the wrong size on the wrong axle.
variants.safety_warning: Never mix sizes against the placard or stagger map.

steps.title: Rotate or swap the set
steps.description: Follow your manual's pattern (often forward-cross or rearward-cross for AWD). For seasonal sets, keep each wheel's position marked. Torque lugs to placard spec in a star pattern after the car is down.
steps.safety_warning: Jack stands before removing wheels. Re-torque after 25–50 miles. If TPMS won't relearn, a shop tool may be needed — safe to drive if pressures are correct and only the light remains.

action_buttons.label: Which rotation pattern?
action_buttons.payload: What tire rotation pattern should I use for my drivetrain and tire sizes?

action_buttons.label: Stuck lug / seized wheel
action_buttons.payload: A lug nut or wheel is seized during tire work. Safe next steps?

variants.description: AWD/4WD: stay within manufacturer tread-depth match rules across axles — big mismatches can stress the transfer case.

steps.title: Store the off-season set & log it
steps.description: Bag off-season tires cool and dry, bagged if possible. Log today's pressures, tread readings, and mileage so the next rotation is easy.

completion.title: Tires checked — grip unlocked
completion.description: Recheck pressures next month and after big temperature swings. Default rotation reminder: ~6,000 miles (we'll align with your oil interval when we can).

action_buttons.label: Ask about noise / pull
action_buttons.payload: My car pulls or tires hum after the check. What should we look at next?
